newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-AMBROSE STRIKES EARLY FOR WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AMBROSE STRIKES EARLY FOR WEST INDIES.

text.p: A three-wicket opening burst by Curtly Ambrose gave Sri Lanka's batsmen a torrid time on the opening day of the inaugural Caribbean test between the sides on Friday.

By lunch, having been put in, the Sri Lankans had staged a partial recovery to reach 72 for three with opener Sanath Jayasuriya unbeaten on 50 but had already discovered the harsh realities of facing West Indian fast bowlers on their own soil.
The experienced Ambrose quickly reduced them to 23 for three, removing opener Roshan Mahanama for one, Russell Arnold for a first-ball duck and Aravinda de Silva, also without scoring.
In the process, Ambrose increased his tally of test wickets to 298 in his 71st test and looked to be enjoying what appeared to be a bouncy pitch.

Mahanama gave wicket-keeper Courtney Browne his 50th test dismissal in his 14th test before Arnold, a late replacement for the injured Marvan Atapattu, fended a lifting delivery to Stuart Williams at third slip.
In his third over, Ambrose then captured the key wicket of De Silva, who was caught at cover point by captain Courtney Walsh cutting at a short delivery.
Jayasuriya, despite giving a chance at 35, showed great resistance and class to reach his fifty off 57 deliveries in 120 minutes with two sixes off pacer Ian Bishop and five fours.
